\chapter{XOR Fundamentals}
\label{ch:xor}

\begin{tcolorbox}[enhanced, colback=white, colframe=secondaryblue, boxrule=1pt, arc=2mm]
\textbf{\large\textcolor{primaryblue}{XOR is addition without carries: it cancels pairs, undoes itself and has a closed form over every range of integers.}}
\end{tcolorbox}

\chapterfacts{900}{1700}{5}{10}{30}

\begin{plannedbox}[Planned Contents --- this chapter is not written yet]
\textbf{Part A --- Lessons}
\begin{enumerate}[leftmargin=*, label=\textbf{A\arabic*.}, itemsep=1pt]
    \item The XOR laws: $x \oplus x = 0$, $x \oplus 0 = x$, associativity, and XOR as addition modulo 2 per bit
    \item XOR of $0..n$ in $\bigO{1}$ (period 4) and of any range $[l, r]$
    \item Undoing XOR: recovering an array from adjacent or prefix XORs
    \item XOR of pairs and triplets: when an equation $a \oplus b = c$ fixes the third value
    \item XOR and parity: what an XOR of everything tells you, and what it hides
\end{enumerate}
